title: Which proportion of cases can be completed purely by clinical examination? Retrospective analysis of diagnostic tests for brain death at Freiburg University Medical center 2012-2025
summary: The determination of brain death (irreversible loss of brain function ≙ ILBF) follows a fixed clinical and technical scheme (i.a. classification according to primary / secondary brain damage, exclusion of reversible causes, one or multiple clinical examination, if necessary diagnostic methods  for example Doppler Sonography or EEG). This study is a retrospective analysis of data from 2012-2025 collected as a part of diagnostic tests for brain death. Main question includes which proportion of cases can be completed purely by multiple clinical examination without any diagnostic methods. Furthermore we examine difficult factors during ILBF diagnosis. These factors involve the proportion of patients who needed a half-sided excision of skull bones (hemicraniectomy) because of their severe brain injury , the proportion of patients who needed an extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO / ECLS) because of severe heart / lung disease, the proportion of patient who showed „phenomena of spinalisation“ as a correlate for the severe brain injury with separation to spinal cord and the number of diagnostic tests for brain death which only can be completed by showing a perfusion arrest (for example Doppler Sonography)and the reasons for that fact.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient who meet the requirements for ILBF diagnosis and were included in the IHA diagnostics from 2012-2025
Exclusion criteria:
no criteria
